text:
Noah: Quick RFC follow-up: instead of a large canonical manifest we could add a tiny adapter-introspection handshake + a very small bridge artifact. Introspection endpoint answers: capabilities, secret_surface, allowed_fallbacks, telemetry_keys. This keeps adapters authoritative while giving infra a predictable contract. Thoughts?

Priya: I like adapter-authorship. Key win: infra doesn't need to know KMS details. But we still want a stable, versioned artifact to validate against in CI. How do we represent schema evolution?

Connor: Proposal: handshake response is a small JSON blob served by adapter during deploy-time only. Schema version annotated as `handshake_v`. Infra validates the blob at commit and stores an immutable copy per deployment. That avoids per-request translation and still centralizes discovery.

Elena: Edgecase: dedicated customers with customized runtime constraints (e.g., forced-quantization profile) need override knobs. Add `overrides_allowed: [list]` and `override_precedence` rules in the handshake. Also require adapters to declare if they honor `overrides_allowed`.

Priya: Observability: require the handshake to include `console_labels` and `redwood_metric_prefix` to ensure consistent dashboards. If adapter doesn't provide, CI should fail with a lint error.

Noah: Security: handshake must not include secrets. Only stable references like `secret_refs: [\"kms:projects/...\", \"local:path\"]`. For private/on-prem deployments, adapters return `airgap: true` and an opt-out flag so infra won't push migration tooling.

Connor: Implementation notes: 1) Add `adapter-introspect` endpoint to adapter API (GET /introspect) returning small JSON; 2) Loader in infra calls endpoint during deploy and stores artifact; 3) Provide `bridge-check` CLI that validates client-side before pushing manifest.

Elena: Perf: calling introspect at deploy time OK. But we should cache artifact and pin it to manifest hash. Also add a background revalidate job that checks adapter schema compatibility monthly for long-lived deployments.

Priya: Rollout: feature flag in infra `adapter_handshake_v1` initially off. Pilot with hosted adapter and one dedicated customer. Add lint rules to new PR template. Provide migration guide showing `old_manifest -> handshake artifact` transformation and example `bridge-check --dry-run`.

ci-bot: ci-bot: PR template updated in infra: https://git.internal/infra/PR-templates/adapter-handshake.md. Validator added to ci-lint.

Noah: One more: fallback arbitration order. Handshake returns an ordered list `fallback_priority`. Infra should honor that order before applying global fallbacks. If adapter omits it, infra should apply default global fallback order.

Connor: Agree. Also include `model_variant_support` list (quantized32, quantized8, fp16) so infra can pick compatible fallbacks.

Elena: Add tests: handshake lint, override precedence matrix, secret_ref mapping smoke-test, telemetry label roundtrip. Also add perf target: handshake fetch + validate < 5ms in typical deploy pipeline.

Priya: I'll update RFC notes and add a minimal handshake example and rollout checklist. If no objections by end of week we'll open POCs for hosted loader and dedicated-adapter branch.

Noah: Thanks all. This keeps adapters in control while giving infra the guardrails we need.
__notes: Slack thread about adding an adapter introspection handshake + small bridge artifact to unify capability discovery and safe migration across hosted/dedicated/private. Chronological, Slack-style short messages.
